scope: Editorial evidence leads for the website; scoped facts, not a fresh live system acceptance.

title.de: Die Daten waren da. Die Bedienung noch nicht.
title.en: The data existed. The experience did not yet.

episodes.problem: Signal K/NMEA solve data exchange, but not the individual touch interaction, stale-data treatment, command confirmation and physical control paths needed for the chosen devices.
episodes.response: Native Android clients consume canonical gateway state. Source timestamps, authority, capabilities and confirmed command results distinguish a responsive local preview from an actual applied hardware state.
episodes.practicalGain: Different screens can reuse the same service contract while presenting a purpose-built instrument/audio/chart experience; integration work becomes reusable.
episodes.limit: This is not proof that every arbitrary device or future service already works. Existing touch-friendly projects such as KIP must be acknowledged rather than declaring all alternatives desktop-only.

title.de: Eine optionale Integration legte die ganze Karte lahm.
title.en: An optional integration stopped the whole chart.

episodes.problem: MAP51 crashed on physical Lumina before renderer startup because the older Home6 lacked an optional content provider; the same APK had the provider available in the Home11 emulator environment.
episodes.response: MAP52 made observer registration optional, retried when the provider became available and retained the protected config path. The exact SecurityException path was reproduced in regression tests.
episodes.practicalGain: A missing optional Home integration no longer needs to prevent local chart startup. This illustrates why local rendering and optional service integration should be separable.
episodes.limit: The contemporaneous fix report proved host regression behavior and artifact identity, not a successful fresh physical startup. Later physical MAP evidence belongs to its own versions.

title.de: Android 14 auf dem Karton war Android 10 im Gerät.
title.en: The Android 14 label hid an Android 10 platform.

episodes.problem: Lumina2 displayed Android14 because an OEM file and framework override substituted the version string. Native properties, Settings package and actual interface level established Android10/API29.
episodes.response: Compatibility and native tests target API29 rather than relying on the marketing/version display. The investigation was read-only and retained exact firmware binding.
episodes.practicalGain: Cheap hardware can be useful when its actual platform is understood; the recovery recipe captures that knowledge instead of making each builder rediscover it.
episodes.limit: Do not generalize this vendor mechanism to every inexpensive Android product. Only the investigated devices and bindings are evidenced.

title.de: Gleiches Display heißt nicht gleiche Firmware.
title.en: The same display does not mean the same firmware.

episodes.problem: Both Luminas report the same UIS8581A/PowerVR GE8322 base, 4GiB class, 64GB class and 2000×1200 surface, yet flash product/firmware identities and OEM software differ. OEM knob/start behavior therefore cannot simply share one unchecked profile.
episodes.response: Device-bound control/start profiles, actual rotary/short/long input cases and a real boot with No5 Home, Control and GPS were retained. Lumina2 has eight actual MAP input cases in the accepted source chain.
episodes.practicalGain: The path from bargain display to integrated control position becomes a repeatable, versioned setup instead of a one-off configuration.
episodes.limit: The base hardware report is not a full bill of materials, sunlight/waterproof test or complete long-run stability acceptance. 75 euros remains Christoph's stated device price, not an invoice-verified installed-system cost.

title.de: Schneller zeichnen, ohne die Karte auszudünnen.
title.en: Draw with less overhead without thinning the chart.

episodes.problem: Early chart rendering had costly draw submission and repeated shader lookups. Performance symptoms differed between emulators, software GL and the physical Android GPU, so a desktop result could not substitute for device evidence.
episodes.response: Bounded batching preserved original vertices/order and fallback paths. Uniform/attribute locations were cached with context/program lifecycle rules. Frame sequences were compared byte-for-byte against the preserved renderer.
episodes.practicalGain: The optimization target is redundant work, while chart content and safety portrayal retain an explicit comparison baseline. The device's GPU can be used locally without shipping a rendered desktop screen.
episodes.limit: The original reports establish reduced submission/query counts and unchanged comparison pixels; they explicitly do not establish a universal FPS gain or measured GPU time. Do not reuse those counts as a physical speed claim.

title.de: Ein Zoomfinger darf keinen Button auslösen.
title.en: A zooming finger must not trigger a button.

episodes.problem: A native chart surface and overlaid Compose controls share touch input. During a pinch/rotation, a second finger could encounter controls in the short interval before the UI redraw removed them; Android system gestures impose their own edge constraints.
episodes.response: Touch ownership, gesture masks and lifecycle cancellation were made explicit. Buttons and dock disappear during accepted map touch, the native tracker retains complete pointer events, and a bounded edge gesture opens the dock outside protected zones.
episodes.practicalGain: A deliberately designed touch surface needs integration across controls, gestures and Android lifecycle, not simply larger desktop buttons.
episodes.limit: The cited regression includes actual MotionEvent paths and native test pixels, but its documented OEM/system-navigation check remains separately scoped.

title.de: Drei Lautstärkeregler brauchen eine gemeinsame Wahrheit.
title.en: Three volume controls need one common truth.

episodes.problem: Spotify Connect, screen faders and physical knobs could otherwise each carry their own gain or stale target. A smooth animation alone would not say whether the Pi actually applied a value.
episodes.response: The retained audio path moves receiver and HELM Main control onto the same Camilla gain and confirms commands against state revisions. WSS sends bounded/coalesced fader updates; stale leases and uncertain replies are not replayed. The source records the actual HTTP-to-WSS transitions rather than treating an async label as proof of a stream.
episodes.practicalGain: Multiple control positions can share one actual volume state instead of multiplying volume stages. This is a concrete foundation for another knob or client.
episodes.limit: The historical HELM84 physical run confirmed174/174 WSS commands; this is not a fresh complete two-client audible latency or current long-run acceptance. New radio/wired remotes still need their own adapter and device validation.

title.de: Die Kurve war richtig. Die Bedienung noch nicht schnell genug.
title.en: The curve was right. Editing was not yet fast enough.

episodes.problem: EQ projection could require substantial Pi compute, while the physical Android edit gesture still showed long revision gaps and missed frame budgets. Correct coefficients did not by themselves make editing fluid.
episodes.response: The native projection reused exact unchanged ratios/results in bounded caches while retaining the same search/grid/validity contract. Confirmed values and the visible curve are kept distinct from optimistic input.
episodes.practicalGain: The shared Pi service can do careful sound processing once while clients focus on interaction. Actual bottlenecks are measured rather than solved by merely purchasing a more expensive display.
episodes.limit: Short21Oct Pi runs improved ordinary16-point median confirmation166→116ms and constrained957→93ms under documented conditions. A3749.5ms outlier remains. The HELM143 fluid-editing acceptance remains FAIL; screenshots do not override it, and no universal latency/acoustic claim is warranted.

title.de: Routen gehören in einen vorhandenen Standard.
title.en: Routes belong in an existing standard.

episodes.problem: A chart editor alone does not provide persistent shared routes, safe offline drafts or protection against conflicting changes.
episodes.response: Signal K resources remain the route authority; the gateway exposes authenticated route operations and MAP separates local drafts from an origin-bound confirmed cache. The actual native workspace shows a schematic coordinate editor that remains usable without a loaded chart.
episodes.practicalGain: Route work reuses the same backend foundation rather than creating another incompatible route silo.
episodes.limit: The25Oct native route screenshot is a local test-route edit. Its remote save/delete attempt returned503 and must not be presented as fully accepted route synchronization.

title.de: 20Hz war ein Messproblem, kein neuer Anzeigewert.
title.en: 20Hz was a measurement problem, not a new display number.

episodes.problem: A cheap fishfinder's display/update cycle does not expose a high-rate qualified sonar. A captured waveform is not enough without a real transmit reference, echo qualification and usable depth window.
episodes.response: Pico acquisition, own transmit control, physical markers and raw-ping identity were bound through the pipeline. The documented600-second16Oct trial retained8807own starts/markers/raw pings and8502usable detections; five-second usable rates ranged6.4–19.6Hz, mean14.17Hz.
episodes.practicalGain: The experiment moves beyond reading a slow LCD: the same measurement stream can feed an own echogram and depth service, independently of the display chosen.
episodes.limit: Depth-dependent trial on one investigated fishfinder, no arbitrary-fishfinder compatibility or sustained20Hz at all depths. Absolute depth calibration, later continuity failures and boat-installation acceptance remain separate. Temperature investigation exists, but no complete real temperature chain was proven by these selected media.
